label: late original-phase c / <DEL> in long sequences (often starting with q)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.004% of steps). Fires only at t=5..9, at the end of the original phase or on the delimiter, almost only in long sequences (L=8-9, 97% of mass). Two contexts: (1) input c as the last or second-to-last original token (58% of mass, 16x lift), and (2) the <DEL> step (32% of mass), mostly when the sequence starts with q. The largest activations come from sequences that start with q and have o at position 1-2, often with w or r before the c (max 4.6 on q o r o w 2 w c). It never fires in the copy phase or at t<5. The predicate gets about 80% of mass but only ~1% precision: most late c / <DEL> steps in long q-initial sequences stay inactive. Firing seems to need an extra content conjunction (o, w, r, q in the prefix) that I could not capture with a simple predicate. Adding q-first and early-o conditions raises precision to only ~10% and halves recall.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=q (+4.28), orig2=o (+3.10), orig2=r (+2.63), orig1=o (+2.52), orig3=o (+2.52), orig3=r (+2.13). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.07), next_out=- (-2.29), orig6=- (-1.77), orig8=- (-1.38).
